what_this_is: The 200-step timing slice on the RTX 3060 Ti that WORK_PLAN.md section 8 asks for per Stage 3 arm. Both SciBERT arms were trained on Apple Silicon (MPS), so this is the only measurement of them on the project's CUDA device. It is a timing benchmark only: no checkpoint from these runs is used anywhere, and no reported metric comes from them.

comparison_with_the_training_machine.note: The reported runs trained on MPS. Wall-clock per step is directly comparable; the memory figures are NOT. peak_cuda_allocated_mb is what the CUDA allocator held, whereas the MPS runs recorded an estimate of shared unified memory (~10 GB), which includes memory the allocator did not own.

not_measured_here: The majority and TF-IDF baselines take no gradient steps. Both are sklearn fits (OneVsRestClassifier over LogisticRegression, scripts/baselines.py:384-393), so a per-step figure does not exist for them and section 8's per-arm wording does not apply. Their compute cost is a single fit wall-clock plus peak host memory, which belongs in their own run log.
